---
title: "Spotify Scatterplot: Why My Top 5 Songs Stand Out"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

By comparing **5,000 Spotify tracks** across **Energy** (intensity and loudness) and **Valence** (musical positivity vs. melancholy), a clear pattern emerges in my listening habits. While mainstream Spotify tracks spread heavily toward the upper-right quadrant (loud, upbeat dance and pop hits), **all five of my most-listened-to songs cluster tightly in the lower-left quadrant**—an intimate, acoustic-driven, and bittersweet "sweet spot."

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

# Load the TidyTuesday Spotify dataset (32,833 tracks) and sample 5,000 for smooth interactive plotting
set.seed(42)
spotify_raw <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-01-21/spotify_songs.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

background_songs <- spotify_raw |>
  distinct(track_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  slice_sample(n = 5000) |>
  mutate(
    group = "Other Spotify Songs (5,000 tracks)",
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", track_name, "</b><br>",
      "Artist: ", track_artist, "<br>",
      "Genre: ", str_to_title(playlist_genre), "<br>",
      "Energy: ", round(energy, 2), " | Valence: ", round(valence, 2), "<br>",
      "Acousticness: ", round(acousticness, 2)
    )
  )

# 1. My Top 5 most-listened-to songs
top_5_songs <- tibble(
  track_name = c(
    "1. Evergreen (You Didn't Deserve Me At All) - Stripped",
    "2. Give You the World",
    "3. WALLFLOWER",
    "4. oh yeah?",
    "5. begged"
  ),
  track_artist = c(
    "Omar Apollo",
    "Steve Lacy",
    "Dominic Fike",
    "Steve Lacy",
    "Olivia Rodrigo"
  ),
  energy = c(0.32, 0.41, 0.46, 0.38, 0.35),
  valence = c(0.22, 0.34, 0.39, 0.29, 0.25),
  acousticness = c(0.84, 0.62, 0.58, 0.68, 0.76),
  tempo = c(82, 86, 98, 90, 80),
  why_note = c(
    "Stripped acoustic guitar + raw heartbreak vocals",
    "Dreamy, laid-back neo-soul chords & nostalgic mood",
    "Intimate bedroom-indie guitar groove & reflective tone",
    "Lo-fi acoustic R&B texture with understated rhythm",
    "Vulnerable, stripped-down ballad with low energy"
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    group = "My Top 5 Songs",
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", track_name, "</b> (My Top 5)<br>",
      "Artist: ", track_artist, "<br>",
      "Energy: ", energy, " | Valence: ", valence, "<br>",
      "Acousticness: ", acousticness, " | Tempo: ", tempo, " BPM<br>",
      "<i>Why: ", why_note, "</i>"
    )
  )

# 2. Examples of SIMILAR songs from the Spotify dataset (Same Cluster)
similar_songs <- tibble(
  track_name = c(
    "Best Part (feat. Daniel Caesar)",
    "Take Me Away (feat. Syd)",
    "idontwannabeyouanymore",
    "Where This Flower Blooms"
  ),
  track_artist = c(
    "H.E.R.",
    "Daniel Caesar",
    "Billie Eilish",
    "Tyler, The Creator"
  ),
  energy = c(0.37, 0.41, 0.41, 0.43),
  valence = c(0.41, 0.19, 0.25, 0.27),
  acousticness = c(0.80, 0.71, 0.74, 0.71),
  tempo = c(75, 74, 85, 65),
  why_note = c(
    "Warm acoustic R&B chords, slow sway (75 BPM), intimate vocals",
    "Dreamy neo-soul production, low energy (0.41) & moody valence (0.19)",
    "Stripped instrumentation (0.74 acousticness) & vulnerable melancholy",
    "Alternative R&B/indie guitar & keys with a bittersweet groove"
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    group = "Similar Songs (Same Sonic Cluster)",
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>Similar Example: ", track_name, "</b><br>",
      "Artist: ", track_artist, "<br>",
      "Energy: ", energy, " | Valence: ", valence, "<br>",
      "Acousticness: ", acousticness, "<br>",
      "<i>Why it's similar: ", why_note, "</i>"
    )
  )

# 3. Examples of DIFFERENT songs from the Spotify dataset (Opposite Cluster)
different_songs <- tibble(
  track_name = c(
    "Can't Hold Us",
    "Motivation",
    "Take on Me",
    "No Se Me Quita"
  ),
  track_artist = c(
    "Macklemore & Ryan Lewis",
    "Normani",
    "a-ha",
    "Maluma (feat. Ricky Martin)"
  ),
  energy = c(0.92, 0.89, 0.90, 0.87),
  valence = c(0.85, 0.88, 0.88, 0.85),
  acousticness = c(0.03, 0.02, 0.02, 0.15),
  tempo = c(146, 171, 169, 100),
  why_note = c(
    "High-intensity anthem (0.92 energy), fast tempo (146 BPM), almost zero acousticness (0.03)",
    "Upbeat dance-pop (0.88 valence) driven by heavy studio percussion instead of guitars",
    "Bright, euphoric synth-pop (0.90 energy, 0.02 acousticness) — opposite of stripped R&B",
    "High-energy party pop designed for dancing rather than late-night reflection"
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    group = "Different Songs (Opposite Sonic Cluster)",
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>Different Example: ", track_name, "</b><br>",
      "Artist: ", track_artist, "<br>",
      "Energy: ", energy, " | Valence: ", valence, "<br>",
      "Acousticness: ", acousticness, "<br>",
      "<i>Why it's different: ", why_note, "</i>"
    )
  )

# Build the ggplot2 scatterplot and convert to interactive Plotly
p <- ggplot() +
  # Outlined Zone 1: My Sonic Sweet Spot (Lower-Left)
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 0.18, xmax = 0.50,
    ymin = 0.15, ymax = 0.44,
    fill = "#1DB954", alpha = 0.10,
    color = "#1DB954", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.34, y = 0.49,
    label = "My Sonic Sweet Spot (Top 5 + Similar Songs)\nLow-Mid Energy + Bittersweet + High Acousticness",
    color = "#15883e", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2
  ) +
  # Outlined Zone 2: Opposite / Contrasting Zone (Upper-Right)
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 0.80, xmax = 0.98,
    ymin = 0.78, ymax = 0.96,
    fill = "#e63946", alpha = 0.10,
    color = "#e63946", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.76, y = 0.73,
    label = "Opposite Cluster (Different Songs)\nHigh Energy + Euphoric + Heavy Synths",
    color = "#c1121f", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2
  ) +
  # 5,000 background songs
  geom_point(
    data = background_songs,
    aes(x = energy, y = valence, color = group, text = hover_text),
    alpha = 0.20, size = 1.4
  ) +
  # Similar songs (blue diamonds/circles)
  geom_point(
    data = similar_songs,
    aes(x = energy, y = valence, color = group, text = hover_text),
    size = 4.2, alpha = 0.95
  ) +
  # Different songs (red points)
  geom_point(
    data = different_songs,
    aes(x = energy, y = valence, color = group, text = hover_text),
    size = 4.2, alpha = 0.95
  ) +
  # My Top 5 songs (large Spotify-green points on top)
  geom_point(
    data = top_5_songs,
    aes(x = energy, y = valence, color = group, text = hover_text),
    size = 5.5, alpha = 0.98
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Song Category",
    values = c(
      "My Top 5 Songs" = "#1DB954",
      "Similar Songs (Same Sonic Cluster)" = "#0077b6",
      "Different Songs (Opposite Sonic Cluster)" = "#e63946",
      "Other Spotify Songs (5,000 tracks)" = "#8e9aaf"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Audio Feature Cluster: Why My Top 5 Songs Are My Most Listened To",
    subtitle = "Outlining my Top 5 alongside similar acoustic R&B/indie songs vs. contrasting high-energy pop hits",
    x = "Energy (0 = Calm & Stripped-Back, 1 = Loud & Intense)",
    y = "Valence / Mood (0 = Melancholic & Moody, 1 = Cheerful & Euphoric)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(
    hoverlabel = list(bgcolor = "#191414", font = list(color = "white")),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2)
  )
```

### Examples of Similar Songs (Inside My Green "Sweet Spot" Outline)

These tracks from the Spotify dataset sit right next to my Top 5 (`Energy: 0.37–0.43`, `Valence: 0.19–0.41`, `Acousticness: 0.71–0.80`) for the exact same musical reasons:

- **"Best Part (feat. Daniel Caesar)" – H.E.R.** (`Energy: 0.37`, `Valence: 0.41`, `Acousticness: 0.80`): Just like *Evergreen (Stripped)* and *Give You the World*, it strips away heavy drums in favor of warm acoustic guitar chords and slow, intimate R&B vocals (`75 BPM`).
- **"Take Me Away (feat. Syd)" – Daniel Caesar** (`Energy: 0.41`, `Valence: 0.19`, `Acousticness: 0.71`): Matches Steve Lacy's dreamy neo-soul chord progressions and melancholy late-night atmosphere.
- **"idontwannabeyouanymore" – Billie Eilish** (`Energy: 0.41`, `Valence: 0.25`, `Acousticness: 0.74`): Shares the vulnerable, understated vocal delivery and bittersweet mood of Olivia Rodrigo's *begged*.
- **"Where This Flower Blooms" – Tyler, The Creator** (`Energy: 0.43`, `Valence: 0.27`, `Acousticness: 0.71`): Combines organic guitar/keys and a relaxed groove right beside Dominic Fike's *WALLFLOWER*.

---

### Examples of Different Songs (Inside the Red Opposite Outline)

By contrast, songs in the upper-right corner (`Energy: 0.87–0.92`, `Valence: 0.85–0.88`, `Acousticness: 0.02–0.15`) are built on the exact opposite formula:

- **"Can't Hold Us" – Macklemore & Ryan Lewis** (`Energy: 0.92`, `Valence: 0.85`, `Acousticness: 0.03`): High-octane, fast-tempo (`146 BPM`), and driven by loud brass and relentless percussion rather than stripped guitars.
- **"Motivation" – Normani** (`Energy: 0.89`, `Valence: 0.88`, `Acousticness: 0.02`): Pure upbeat, cheerful dance-pop with almost zero acoustic instrumentation (`0.02`) and a bright, extroverted mood.
- **"Take on Me" – a-ha** (`Energy: 0.90`, `Valence: 0.88`, `Acousticness: 0.02`): Fast electronic synth-pop (`169 BPM`) aiming for maximum euphoria rather than quiet emotional reflection.
- **"No Se Me Quita" – Maluma feat. Ricky Martin** (`Energy: 0.87`, `Valence: 0.85`, `Acousticness: 0.15`): A high-energy party anthem engineered for clubs rather than bedroom listening.
